newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Canada closer to resuming salmon talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Canada closer to resuming salmon talks.

text.p: U.S. and Canada are "a step closer" to resuming stalled talks over fishing rights after an emergency meeting on their dispute over the Pacific salmon catch, the State Department said Wedndesday.
"Both sides are looking at a way to get to negotiations. We are looking at a facilitating mechanism that would be a step toward this," spokesman Jim Foley told reporters.

Foley said Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy had requested a high-level meeting Tuesday after Canadian fishermen held an Alaskan ferry captive in Prince Rupert, British Columbia, for three days to protest against alleged U.S. overfishing of salmon in the Pacific.
The Canadian fishermen contend that Alaskans have taken almost four times as much sockeye salmon this season as allowed under a 1985 Pacific Salmon treaty.
"Both nations felt it was imperative to speak directly at a high level," Foley said.

He described the hour-long meeting as "very good and friendly" and said Axworthy and U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott agreed on the importance of saving the treaty and discussed the need to reinvigorate the process. Foley declined to say what the "facilitating mechanism" might be but said it would bring the two countries "a step closer" to resuming talks.
